page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. Built on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture, this instance features 96 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 5700 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD instance store capacity. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance and memory subsystem efficiency. The instance achieves top-tier status in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core workloads, including software compilation and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, scoring in the top 10% for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read/write operations. In database and key-value store workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier performance, particularly in Redis SET operations and Passmark database operations. It also shows strong capabilities in text processing and medium-to-large LLM text generation, though single-threaded tasks and small-model text generation show average to weak relative performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8gd.24xlarge offers a high density of memory and local NVMe storage per vCPU, making it a viable alternative to x86-based memory-optimized instances for workloads optimized for the ARM64 architecture. The lack of hyperthreading means each of the 96 vCPUs is a dedicated physical core, reducing resource contention. This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads, including large-scale relational and non-relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, high-throughput static web serving, and data-intensive software compilation pipelines.
